description: Non-AI path-consumer annotations (plan §2.3/§1.5): recorded evidence for every production consumer that can spawn a process (dynamicPathConsumption — a spawned process consumes paths the static scanner cannot resolve, so it fails closed without this evidence) and for every consumer added, removed, or whose per-signal call-site profile changed since the immutable pre-gate snapshot (workflow-path-consumer-pregate-v1.json). Verified by scripts/verifyWorkflowPathConsumers.mjs: a child_process consumer without a dynamicPathConsumption entry fails, a stale sourceSpan or stability digest fails, and an annotation matching no live consumer/drift fails.

annotations.rationale: cp.execFile("git", ["rev-parse", …]) repository checks (isGitWorkspace and siblings) run with the workspace root as cwd during review/publish flows. Arguments are fixed git subcommands; the only path consumed is the cwd, never a task-artifact or Chat-private path. Spawned git can read repository state, so it stays inventoried until the privacy classifier bounds it.

cp.execFile("git", …) used to consult/update ignore state for the Ensemble meta-resources folder; fixed git subcommands with the workspace root as cwd plus the meta-resources relative path. No Chat-private or provider data reaches the spawned process.

The CLI provider runner spawns configured agent CLIs (plus where.exe/which resolution, auth checks, and process-tree cleanup) and hands them workspace/task paths by design — the definitional unresolved dynamic consumer. Plan boundaries already constrain it: general-workspace CLI processes are unsupported for preflight/edit execution, CLI runners are excluded from edit execution, and the runnerV1 cohort replaces its artifact-destination protocol with bounded stdout capture (no artifact/result path in any V1 request, AC-RUNNER-01/02).

Spawns CLI provider model-listing commands (cp.spawn with manual timeout + killProcessTree). Command and arguments come from static provider definitions; no task or workspace paths are passed. Inventoried because a spawned process can still read the environment it runs in.
Spawns taskkill for process-tree termination of CLI provider children; arguments are PIDs only, never paths.

Spawns package-manager check scripts (verified checks: locator resolution via execFileSync, then spawn of pnpm/npm run … in the publish-scope cwd). Consumes workspace-root/publish-scope paths as cwd; spawned checks can read the whole workspace, which is why the row also carries diagnostics/artifactReadWrite sinks and stays behind this evidence until the classifier lands.

OS desktop-notification helper (cp.execFile of the platform notifier with a 15s timeout). Arguments are notification title/body strings; sanitized-diagnostics classification applies to what may enter them — no paths or private payloads are passed.

Spawns git for repository info (branch/remote discovery) with the workspace root as cwd and fixed subcommands; feeds Commit/Push and publish-scope decisions. The git cohort's index/privacy checks (§2.4) are the enforcement point for what may be staged.

The Safety cohort replaced both recoverCompletedTaskCreations() call sites (activation and the in-command promotion pass) with consultation of LegacyCreatingStartupGateV0's published read-only classification, moving the creation-footprint reads into the gate module — the file's workspace.fs call-site profile dropped from 7 to 5 sites. No new consumption was added here.

New Safety-cohort module: the read-only classification pass over legacy `creating` footprints (classifyMetaRoot reads meta-root directory entries and task-progress bytes via workspace.fs at two sites). It performs no writes, no promotion, no ownership adoption, and no provider invocation; superseded by TaskCreationStartupReconcilerV1 in the creation cohort.

Chat cohort, executable-order step 8: activate() now creates the extension's global-storage directory via vscode.workspace.fs.createDirectory(context.globalStorageUri) before configuring the workflow private-storage root — VS Code does not create that directory automatically, and the private-storage root (chat-transactions/, chat-recovery/) is provisioned under it. Best-effort (logs and continues on failure); no task or Chat-private path is involved, only the extension's own storage directory.

annotations.rationale: Foundations cohort, executable-order step 6: the one filesystem mutation surface every workflow consumer (task-local Chat, the durable Chat transaction store) uses — exclusive creation, revision-guarded replacement, bounded reads, nonrecursive directory create/remove, exact-file unlink. Imports node:fs directly; this is the API-touching module the plan's consumer inventory expects other workflow modules (chatHistoryStore.ts, chatInteractionTransactionStoreV1.ts) to be covered transitively through, per this file's own "Known mechanical bound" note.

annotations.rationale: Chat cohort, executable-order step 8: this module's task-local chat-v1.json reads/writes no longer call vscode.workspace.fs directly (the pregate snapshot's two call sites in chatHistoryFileExists/readChatHistory) — every filesystem operation now goes exclusively through the shared WorkflowFileStoreV1 (its own consumer row, src/services/workflowFileStoreV1.ts), reached via workflowRuntimeServicesV1.ts's registered task-folder root. This module now only passes locators/paths to that store, matching the inventory's documented mechanical bound: a module with no fs/workspace.fs API of its own is covered transitively by the consumer module it calls.
